input.rationale: Section 11.5 is the only limitation-of-liability provision: a mutual waiver of indirect and consequential damages with carve-outs, but with no monetary cap. Searches for aggregate liability, shall not exceed, and in no event surface no cap anywhere in the Agreement; the only limits are the insurance minima in Section 11.6. Both Parties direct liability is therefore unlimited, so the clause fails the fallback on a material term (no mutual cap based on 12 months of fees). We target the fallback: one inserted sentence adds a mutual cap at twelve months fees with indemnification, Article 9 confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct expressly outside the cap. We did not add the preferred USD 1,000,000 floor, data-protection or IP-infringement carve-outs, or the payment-obligations exclusion, as those sit above the fallback threshold; fraud already sits outside the 11.5 waiver.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement waives consequential damages but contains no aggregate liability cap, leaving both Parties exposed without limit. We added a mutual cap at twelve months' fees, with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct sitting outside the cap.

ops.text: Cap on Liability. Except for (a) a Party's indemnification obligations under this Article 11, (b) a Party's breach of its obligations under Article 9, and (c) a Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by AbbVie under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim.
